opportunity_description: A SaaS analytics platform providing real-time student engagement and learning outcome dashboards for European business schools. The platform integrates with existing LMS systems (Moodle, Canvas, Blackboard) to aggregate behavioural data and produce actionable insights for programme directors and faculty. The core value proposition is reducing student dropout rates by 15-25% through early intervention triggered by engagement pattern detection.
competitive_strategy: Differentiate through deep specialisation in business school pedagogy rather than competing as a generic EdTech analytics platform. Build switching costs via proprietary benchmarking data across the European business school network.

icp_hypothesis.buyer_role: Dean of Programmes or Director of Digital Learning
icp_hypothesis.budget_process: Annual budget cycle, typically approved Q4 for next academic year. Procurement via university purchasing if >20k EUR.
icp_hypothesis.decision_timeline: 3-6 months from first demo to signed contract due to academic committee approval requirements
pain_points: High student dropout rates impacting rankings
No visibility into engagement until exam results arrive
AMBA/EQUIS accreditation pressure for learning outcome evidence
Faculty resistance to adopting new tools without clear benefit data

assumptions_used.statement: European business schools are under accreditation pressure to demonstrate learning outcomes
8 pilot schools achievable in Year 1 given existing network
assumptions_used.source_detail: Alex has contacts at 12 schools from prior career

assumptions_used.statement: 15-25% dropout reduction is achievable with early intervention
assumptions_used.source_detail: Based on published case studies from Civitas Learning and similar platforms

assumptions_used.statement: LMS integration is technically feasible within 3 months per school

uncertainties: GDPR compliance cost for student behavioural data across EU jurisdictions
Whether business schools will share benchmarking data with each other
Technical complexity of legacy LMS integrations at older institutions
